name: oc-be-tools
description: Backend development toolkit for Opencell Core — agents for building entities, services, APIs, tests, and Postman collections, guideline-loading skills, an implementation orchestrator (/oc-be-implement) whose sub-agents record file manifests, an isolated, reproducible two-axis code review (/oc-be-review): fresh headless runs with no conversation, user memory or personal settings, pinned to opus/high, judging a frozen bundle (diff, ticket items split by script, agreed scope, rule catalogue, mechanical checks) with the verdict computed by script, plus a SonarQube summary, enforced before Claude's commits and before AI-usage recording, tagging the ticket ai_code_review_back, and an AI-usage estimator (/oc-be-calculate-ai-use) with per-category line/contribution/retention breakdowns, unit-test counts and Postman verification-request / business-assertion counts (plain HTTP-status checks excluded), reviewer-rework provenance, developer-interaction counts, a planning/analysis effort axis, ai_Dev_back / ai_test_back_dev Jira tagging, and a machine-readable JSON record (per domain/user) stored in a dedicated field for reporting. Hooks give ad-hoc work (bugs, enablers worked out in conversation without /oc-be-implement) the same outcomes: an analysis checkpoint (agreed approach, acceptance, deliverables) and per-layer guideline loading before the first edit, capture of script-made edits for the AI-usage metrics, review -> record AI usage -> commit suggested at milestones (tests green, Claude's git commit), and committed work from Claude, the IDE or a terminal offered for recording and merged incrementally into the ticket's record
